title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a hand computation of the smallest regular, i.e. Galois, genus-0 dessin with all branching indices 2: the Klein four-group cover of P^1 branched over 0, 1, ∞. The previous page tabulates automorphism groups of regular polyhedral maps (D5×Z/2, S3×Z/2, Z/2×Z/2, ...), and this page works out the degenerate dihedral case D2 = V4 by hand.

The tower is X_2 --(z↦z^2)--> X_1 --> X_0, where X_0 = P^1 with marked points 0, 1, ∞.

The table aligns the points as follows.
- X_1 → X_0 sends 0|∞ ↦ ∞, 1 ↦ 0, −1 ↦ 1.
- This fixes the map as g(z) = −(z−1)^2/(4z).
- The top-right computation −(1/(4i))(i−1)^2 = 1/2, with (i−1)^2 = −1+1−2i = −2i worked out beside it, is the evaluation g(i) = 1/2.
- g is invariant under the deck involution z ↦ 1/z. The note '1/z ⟷ i, −i' records that this involution swaps the two preimages ±i of 1/2.
- g is a double cover branched at z = 1 (over 0) and z = −1 (over 1). The points 0 and ∞ lie unramified over ∞.

The left column identity −4z/(z−1)^2 = 1 − ((z+1)/(z−1))^2, verified via ((z+1)^2 − (z−1)^2)/(z−1)^2, factors 1/g as follows.
- First apply the Möbius map φ(z) = (z+1)/(z−1).
- Then square, then apply w ↦ 1−w.
- The upside-down block lists the values of φ: 0↦−1, 1↦∞, ∞↦1, −1↦0, i↦−i. φ is an involution, and it moves the branch points ±1 to 0 and ∞.
- So every map in the tower is written as a Möbius-conjugate of z ↦ z^2.

The upside-down diagram 'X_0 ← X_1 ⇐ X_1' with (0,1,∞) ↦ (∞,1,0) seems to redo the same tower in another normalization. The note '1 = f∘f∘f' seems to refer to the order-3 Möbius symmetry permuting 0, 1, ∞.

The composite X_2 → X_0 is z ↦ −(z^2−1)^2/(4z^2), of degree 4.
- Over 0 lie ±1, over 1 lie ±i, over ∞ lie 0 and ∞, each with ramification index 2.
- The cover is Galois with group Z/2×Z/2, generated by z ↦ −z and z ↦ 1/z.

The drawings are the dessins (preimages of the segment [0,1]).
- On X_1, g(e^{iθ}) = sin^2(θ/2), so the preimage is the unit circle: one black vertex at 1, one white vertex at −1, two edges, with 0 and ∞ as face centres. This is the ellipse/sphere picture.
- On X_2, the preimage is again the unit circle, now with black vertices ±1 and white vertices ±i: a 4-cycle (the 'dihedron'), with faces centred at 0 and ∞.
- The triangulated quadrilateral with vertices ∞, 1, 0 and hatched triangles is the standard black/white triangulation of P^1 cut out by the real line, i.e. the 'cellular' description of the cover.

The six points 0, ∞, ±1, ±i are the octahedron vertices. X_2 → X_0 is the classical level-4-over-level-2 modular cover X(4) → X(2) (λ-line), and X_1 → X_0 is, up to sign and inversion, the Landen-type quadratic transformation. The purpose of the page is evidently to have explicit equations and pictures for the V4/dihedral entry of the regular-map table on the previous page, within the Teichmüller-groupoid notes.
errors: No substantive errors. The identity 1 − ((z+1)/(z−1))^2 = −4z/(z−1)^2 is correct, and −(i−1)^2/(4i) = 1/2 is correct.

Minor inconsistency of normalization: the table uses g = −(z−1)^2/(4z), while the left-column identity computes 1/g = −4z/(z−1)^2. Grothendieck seems aware of this, since the upside-down block re-normalizes with (0,1,∞) ↦ (∞,1,0).

ideas.what: Explicit Z/2×Z/2 Galois cover of P^1 branched over 0, 1, ∞ with all indices 2, as a tower of two quadratic maps, and its dessin (a 4-cycle on the sphere)
ideas.modern_name: Regular dessin d'enfant of type (2,2,2) / dihedral map D2; equivalently the modular cover X(4) → X(2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein (octahedral/level-4 covers); dessin viewpoint: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984), Jones–Singerman (1978) for regular maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses dessins and regular maps in general; this specific example is not known to be published by him

ideas.what: Factorization of degree-2 Belyi maps as Möbius ∘ squaring ∘ Möbius, using φ(z) = (z+1)/(z−1)
ideas.modern_name: Normal form of quadratic rational maps / Landen-type transformation

deep.surprise_reason: A routine explicit verification of the classical V4 (octahedral/level-4) cover of the λ-line and its dessin. It is useful as context for the regular-map table on the previous page, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Top right: '−1+1−2i' is the expansion of (i−1)^2 = −2i, written next to i; it is not a separate formula.

Table under the tower: X_2 column lists 0, then '1 −1' (i.e. ±1), then ∞; X_1 column lists 0|∞, 1, −1 (the last overwritten); X_0 column lists ∞, 0, 1. So the rows give the correspondence 0|∞ ↦ ∞, 1 ↦ 0, −1 ↦ 1.
Left column: the upside-down fraction reads −4z/(z−1)^2 = 1 − ((z+1)/(z−1))^2, with the check ((z+1)^2 − (z−1)^2)/(z−1)^2.
Upside-down block: φ(z) = (z+1)/(z−1) with values 0↦−1, ∞↦1, 1↦∞, −1↦0, and '1/z ⟷ i, −i'. The transcription's '0 ↦ ∞' and '0 ↦ 1' lines appear to be reversed readings of these.
The bottom upside-down lines starting 'G_0 —', 'G_1 —' are likely handwritten words (possibly beginning 'Cas'/'Ga...'); they are illegible and probably not the group symbols G_0, G_1.
